game.title: Tutak Bazi
game.description: A game involving small clay whistles shaped like birds or animals, where children compete to create the loudest or most melodic sounds through controlled blowing techniques.
howToPlay: Step 1: Children purchase or make small clay whistles from local potters.
Step 2: Players fill the whistle partially with water to create warbling effects.
Step 3: They take turns blowing into the whistle to produce sounds.
Step 4: Competitions judge who can create the loudest, longest, or most musical sound.
Step 5: Players develop techniques for controlling pitch and volume.
Step 6: Group performances create layered musical effects.
Step 7: Whistles are often decorated with colorful paints.
Step 8: The game teaches breath control and musical appreciation.
Step 9: Broken whistles are replaced with new ones from traveling potters.
Step 10: The tradition connects children to Afghan folk art and craftsmanship.
